sourceHtml:
The ChatGPT desktop app is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US), providing access to OpenAI’s frontier models through two components. Work completes complex, multi-step tasks and delivers review-ready results, and Codex is a coding agent for developing, testing, and reviewing software.

This walkthrough is intended for organizations whose security architecture requires model inference to use AWS GovCloud (US) identities, endpoints, and Regional controls. It configures Codex to route model requests through Amazon Bedrock Mantle in us-gov-west-1, where access can be governed using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and existing AWS GovCloud (US) network controls.

Codex is the OpenAI coding agent for AI-powered software development. With GPT models powering inference, Codex introduces a new class of intelligence optimized for complex, long-horizon developer workflows. You can use the ChatGPT desktop app, the Codex CLI, and IDE integrations with Visual Studio Code, JetBrains, and Xcode. Model inference is routed through the Responses API on Amazon Bedrock.

For customers with data residency requirements, processing stays within the Amazon Bedrock AWS Region that you select. You pay per token with no seat licenses and no per-developer commitments. Zero data retention (ZDR) is also supported. In this configurable mode, prompts and responses are processed without being written to durable storage by AWS or shared with model providers. This helps you protect sensitive information and meet stringent data-governance, privacy, and security requirements.

This post walks through a controlled local deployment of the ChatGPT desktop app that sends model inference to Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-West). The configuration uses API-mode sign-in, a managed device policy, a named AWS profile, and network restrictions. These restrictions allow access only to the approved Amazon Bedrock endpoint while disabling other external connections and network-enabled capabilities. The result is a deployment that an agency security team can test and document before approving broader use.

Using AWS GovCloud (US) and following this guide do not, by themselves, authorize your workload. Your organization remains responsible for reviewing the selected model, AWS services, Region, endpoint, workstation controls, repositories, credentials, and data flows against its system security plan and authorization process.

Solution overview

You can use the ChatGPT desktop app in two ways:

  • Work for larger tasks that need planning, research, files, and a finished result.
  • Codex for technical work such as editing code, running tests, and reviewing pull requests.

The ChatGPT desktop app runs on an organization-managed computer through the desktop app or CLI. It uses the configured AWS credentials to securely send requests to the Amazon Bedrock Mantle endpoint in us-gov-west-1. Because this setup uses AWS directly, ChatGPT workspace rules and user roles don’t control it. The main security controls are the computer’s policies and the AWS identity and permissions being used.

Walkthrough

The configuration has three main steps: set up authentication, set up the ChatGPT desktop app configuration files, and then launch, initialize, and verify the deployment.

Prerequisites

Before setting up the ChatGPT desktop app with AWS GovCloud (US), make sure your version of the ChatGPT desktop app supports Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US). You need an approved AWS GovCloud (US) account, an IAM identity and approved credentials, access to the approved model, AWS Region, and endpoint, and permission to use them. You also need to set up the requirements.toml and config.toml files.

Step 1: Set up authentication

Select the approved AWS GovCloud (US) account and IAM identity or role with access to the approved model in us-gov-west-1. Obtain credentials through your organization’s approved mechanism. This walkthrough uses the named profile codex-il5. Keep credentials, bearer tokens, session tokens, and other secrets out of TOML files.

Protect the profile configuration, credential source, SSO token cache, and any credential helper from ChatGPT desktop app task writes, while allowing approved authentication tools to maintain and refresh credentials.

The ChatGPT desktop app supports two Amazon Bedrock authentication pathways: an Amazon Bedrock API key or the AWS SDK credential chain. AWS SSO through AWS IAM Identity Center is supported within the credential-chain pathway.

The app first checks for AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK in its environment. For desktop use, this variable can be supplied through %USERPROFILE%\.codex\.env on Windows or ~/.codex/.env on Linux and macOS. When present, the bearer token takes precedence over profile-based authentication.

If no bearer token is available, the app falls back to the standard AWS SDK credential chain. The chain can read AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials and related profile settings from ~/.aws/config. On Windows, the corresponding default paths are %USERPROFILE%\.aws\credentials and %USERPROFILE%\.aws\config. The chain also supports SSO profiles. For SSO, it uses the profile settings in the AWS config file and the cached SSO session to obtain temporary role credentials. These credentials don’t need to be manually stored in the AWS credentials file. See OpenAI’s Bedrock authentication documentation and the AWS IAM Identity Center credential provider documentation.

Step 2: Set up ChatGPT desktop app configuration files

You must create two ChatGPT desktop app configuration files: config.toml and requirements.toml.

Important: the configuration files need to be set up before the application is launched. The following table shows the file locations.

Operating system User config.toml Admin requirements.toml
Windows %USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml
Linux ~/.codex/config.toml /etc/codex/requirements.toml
macOS ~/.codex/config.toml /etc/codex/requirements.toml

Start from the requirements.toml file. requirements.toml is an administrator-controlled rules file. It sets security limits that users can’t override, for example, restricting which permission levels, tools, or settings the ChatGPT desktop app is allowed to use.

Use the following baseline for the supported AWS GovCloud (US) Amazon Bedrock deployment. The [windows] section applies only to Windows, and sandbox_private_desktop must be supported by the approved runtime.

allowed_login_methods = ["api"]
allowed_sandbox_modes = ["read-only", "workspace-write"]
allowed_approvals_reviewers = ["user"]
allowed_approval_policies = [
{ granular = { sandbox_approval = false, rules = true,
mcp_elicitations = false, request_permissions = false,
skill_approval = true } },
]
allowed_web_search_modes = ["disabled", "cached"]
allow_browser_and_computer_use = false
allow_appshots = false
allow_remote_control = false
allow_login_shell = false
allow_managed_hooks_only = true
check_for_update_on_startup = false
mcp_servers = {}

[feedback]
enabled = false

[features]
network_proxy = true
in_app_chat = false
in_app_dictation = false
in_app_browser = false
browser_use = false
browser_use_external = false
browser_use_full_cdp_access = false
computer_use = false
in_app_updates = false
image_generation = false
memories = false
chronicle = false
external_agent_memory_import = false
guardian_approval = false
guardianv2 = false
guardian_ext = false
apps = false
enable_mcp_apps = false
plugins = false
remote_plugin = false
plugin_sharing = false
recommended_plugins = false
skill_mcp_dependency_install = false
skill_search = false
workspace_dependencies = false
hooks = false
standalone_web_search = false

[experimental_network]
enabled = true
managed_allowed_domains_only = true
domains = {}
unix_sockets = {}
allow_upstream_proxy = false
dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy = false
dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets = false
allow_local_binding = false

[application.network]
enabled = true

[application.network.domains]
"bedrock-mantle.us-gov-west-1.api.aws" = "allow"
"api.openai.com" = "deny"
"chat.openai.com" = "deny"
"chatgpt.com" = "deny"
"ab.chatgpt.com" = "deny"
"platform.openai.com" = "deny"
"auth.openai.com" = "deny"
"gov.api.openai.com" = "deny"
"gov.chatgpt.com" = "deny"
"sdfedpreastus2.oaiusercontent.com" = "deny"
"o33249.ingest.us.sentry.io" = "deny"
"persistent.oaistatic.com" = "deny"
"oaisidekickupdates.blob.core.windows.net" = "deny"

[windows]
allowed_sandbox_implementations = ["elevated"]
sandbox_private_desktop = true

Next, configure the config.toml file. config.toml tells the ChatGPT desktop app how to operate, including which model provider to use (amazon-bedrock), which model to select, and settings such as permissions or context limits.

Replace the model ID and named profile (for example, codex-il5) with approved values.

model = "REPLACE_WITH_APPROVED_MODEL_ID"
model_provider = "amazon-bedrock"
forced_login_method = "api"
approval_policy = { granular = { sandbox_approval = false,
rules = true, mcp_elicitations = false,
request_permissions = false, skill_approval = true } }
approvals_reviewer = "user"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
web_search = "cached"
allow_login_shell = false
check_for_update_on_startup = false

[model_providers.amazon-bedrock]
base_url = "https://bedrock-mantle.us-gov-west-1.api.aws/openai/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = false
supports_websockets = false
supports_standalone_web_search = false

[model_providers.amazon-bedrock.aws]
region = "us-gov-west-1"
profile = "codex-il5"

[sandbox_workspace_write]
network_access = false

[features]
network_proxy = true

[analytics]
enabled = false

[feedback]
enabled = false

[otel]
exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
log_user_prompt = false

[memories]
generate_memories = false
use_memories = false

[skills.bundled]
enabled = false

[apps._default]
enabled = false

[windows]
sandbox = "elevated"

Step 3: Launch, initialize, and verify

Download the app from the ChatGPT site and install it. Leave the app closed after installation. If it opens automatically or if the app has been launched previously, fully exit ChatGPT and end any lingering ChatGPT or Codex processes.

Make sure requirements.toml and config.toml are in place before the first app launch.

Start the app to load the requirements.toml and config.toml settings. Make sure it shows amazon-bedrock as the model provider.

In the Codex CLI, you should see a /status tab that looks like this:

Figure 1: The Codex CLI /status tab confirming amazon-bedrock as the model provider

In the ChatGPT desktop app, you can also confirm amazon-bedrock as the model provider.

Figure 2: The ChatGPT desktop app settings showing amazon-bedrock as the model provider

Troubleshooting

The application prompts for an OpenAI account. Verify that requirements.toml and config.toml use the exact locations and file names shown in the preceding table, terminate all ChatGPT and Codex processes, and relaunch. The files must precede app launch.

AWS GovCloud (US) endpoint is reported as unsupported. Confirm the exact desktop or app-server release, endpoint, and model with OpenAI. Changing the URL alone does not establish support.

The wrong AWS identity is used. Inspect the effective credential source and named profile. Check whether an Amazon Bedrock API key takes precedence over the profile.

Capability restrictions are missing. Inspect the full effective requirements after restart. The API-only sign-in setting doesn’t apply the capability policy.

Rollback and cleanup

If a validation check fails, stop the rollout. Return the affected devices to the previously approved policy and provider settings, then restart the ChatGPT desktop app. Revoke any temporary AWS credentials or API keys, and confirm that those devices can no longer connect to Amazon Bedrock. Keep a record of the test and clearly document what failed before trying again.

Conclusion

The ChatGPT desktop app on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) gives you a controlled way to use OpenAI frontier models and coding assistance. Inference stays in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. By validating the configuration, confirming the approved AWS identity and endpoint, and verifying security controls, you can confidently prepare the deployment for broader use. This approach supports innovation while aligning deployment decisions with each organization’s security, authorization, and data-handling requirements.

Ready to explore the ChatGPT desktop app with Codex on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)? Start with a controlled deployment, validate your security controls, and work with your security team to prepare for broader adoption.

  • Bedrock AWS GovCloud (US) configuration – ChatGPT desktop app device, provider, network, verification, and troubleshooting guidance.
  • Responses API on Amazon Bedrock – AWS Regions, endpoint behavior, authentication, and permissions for the Responses API.
  • AWS GovCloud (US) compliance – Compliance programs and customer authorization considerations.
  • OpenAI’s Bedrock authentication documentation – Amazon Bedrock API key and AWS SDK credential-chain authentication, including SSO.
  • AWS IAM Identity Center credential provider documentation – SSO profile configuration and temporary AWS credentials.

About the authors

translation.html:
ChatGPT 桌面应用现已在 AWS GovCloud (US) 中的 Amazon Bedrock 上推出，通过两个组件提供对 OpenAI 前沿模型的访问。Work 可完成复杂的多步骤任务，并交付可供审核的成果；Codex 则是用于开发、测试和审查软件的编程智能体。

本操作指南面向安全架构要求模型推理使用 AWS GovCloud (US) 身份、端点和区域级控制措施的组织。它将配置 Codex，使模型请求通过 us-gov-west-1 中的 Amazon Bedrock Mantle 路由，并可使用 AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) 和现有的 AWS GovCloud (US) 网络控制措施来管理访问。

Codex 是 OpenAI 用于 AI 驱动的软件开发的编程智能体。Codex 使用 GPT 模型进行推理，引入了一类针对复杂、长周期开发工作流优化的新型智能能力。你可以使用 ChatGPT 桌面应用、Codex CLI，以及与 Visual Studio Code、JetBrains 和 Xcode 的 IDE 集成。模型推理通过 Amazon Bedrock 上的 Responses API 路由。

对于有数据驻留要求的客户，处理过程始终在你选择的 Amazon Bedrock AWS 区域内进行。你按 token 付费，无需购买席位许可证，也无需作出按开发者计费的承诺。同时支持零数据保留（ZDR）。在这种可配置模式下，提示词和响应在处理过程中不会被 AWS 写入持久存储，也不会与模型提供商共享。这有助于保护敏感信息，并满足严格的数据治理、隐私和安全要求。

本文将介绍如何在受控环境中本地部署 ChatGPT 桌面应用，将模型推理发送到 AWS GovCloud (US-West) 中的 Amazon Bedrock。该配置使用 API 模式登录、受管设备策略、具名 AWS 配置文件和网络限制。这些限制仅允许访问获批的 Amazon Bedrock 端点，同时禁用其他外部连接和需要联网的功能。最终得到的部署可由机构安全团队测试并记录，然后再批准扩大使用范围。

使用 AWS GovCloud (US) 并遵循本指南，本身并不意味着你的工作负载已获得授权。你的组织仍有责任依据其系统安全计划和授权流程，审查所选模型、AWS 服务、区域、端点、工作站控制措施、代码仓库、凭证和数据流。

解决方案概述

你可以通过两种方式使用 ChatGPT 桌面应用：

  • 使用 Work 处理需要规划、研究、文件和最终成果的大型任务。
  • 使用 Codex 处理编辑代码、运行测试和审查拉取请求等技术工作。

ChatGPT 桌面应用通过桌面应用或 CLI 在组织管理的计算机上运行。它使用配置的 AWS 凭证，将请求安全地发送到 us-gov-west-1 中的 Amazon Bedrock Mantle 端点。由于此设置直接使用 AWS，ChatGPT 工作区规则和用户角色无法对其进行控制。主要的安全控制措施是计算机策略，以及所使用的 AWS 身份和权限。

操作指南

配置主要分为三个步骤：设置身份验证，设置 ChatGPT 桌面应用配置文件，然后启动、初始化并验证部署。

前提条件

在为 ChatGPT 桌面应用设置 AWS GovCloud (US) 之前，请确保你使用的 ChatGPT 桌面应用版本支持 AWS GovCloud (US) 中的 Amazon Bedrock。你需要拥有获批的 AWS GovCloud (US) 账户、IAM 身份和获批的凭证，能够访问获批的模型、AWS 区域和端点，并拥有使用它们的权限。你还需要设置 requirements.toml 和 config.toml 文件。

步骤 1：设置身份验证

选择获批的 AWS GovCloud (US) 账户，以及有权访问 us-gov-west-1 中获批模型的 IAM 身份或角色。通过组织批准的机制获取凭证。本操作指南使用具名配置文件 codex-il5。不要将凭证、持有者令牌、会话令牌和其他机密信息放入 TOML 文件。

保护配置文件设置、凭证来源、SSO 令牌缓存和任何凭证辅助工具，防止 ChatGPT 桌面应用任务对其进行写入，同时允许获批的身份验证工具维护和刷新凭证。

ChatGPT 桌面应用支持两种 Amazon Bedrock 身份验证方式：Amazon Bedrock API 密钥或 AWS SDK 凭证链。凭证链方式支持通过 AWS IAM Identity Center 使用 AWS SSO。

应用首先检查其环境中是否存在 AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK。在桌面环境中使用时，可在 Windows 上通过 %USERPROFILE%\.codex\.env 提供此变量，或在 Linux 和 macOS 上通过 ~/.codex/.env 提供。存在此变量时，持有者令牌优先于基于配置文件的身份验证。

如果没有可用的持有者令牌，应用会回退到标准 AWS SDK 凭证链。凭证链可以从 ~/.aws/credentials 读取 AWS 凭证，并从 ~/.aws/config 读取相关配置文件设置。在 Windows 上，对应的默认路径为 %USERPROFILE%\.aws\credentials 和 %USERPROFILE%\.aws\config。凭证链也支持 SSO 配置文件。对于 SSO，它使用 AWS 配置文件中的设置和缓存的 SSO 会话来获取临时角色凭证。这些凭证无需手动存储在 AWS 凭证文件中。请参阅 OpenAI 的 Bedrock 身份验证文档和 AWS IAM Identity Center 凭证提供程序文档。

步骤 2：设置 ChatGPT 桌面应用配置文件

你必须创建两个 ChatGPT 桌面应用配置文件：config.toml 和 requirements.toml。

重要提示：必须在启动应用之前设置好配置文件。下表列出了文件位置。

操作系统 用户 config.toml 管理员 requirements.toml
Windows %USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml
Linux ~/.codex/config.toml /etc/codex/requirements.toml
macOS ~/.codex/config.toml /etc/codex/requirements.toml

先从 requirements.toml 文件开始。requirements.toml 是由管理员控制的规则文件。它设置用户无法覆盖的安全限制，例如限制 ChatGPT 桌面应用可以使用的权限级别、工具或设置。

对于受支持的 AWS GovCloud (US) Amazon Bedrock 部署，请使用以下基线配置。[windows] 部分仅适用于 Windows，且获批的运行时必须支持 sandbox_private_desktop。

接下来，配置 config.toml 文件。config.toml 告诉 ChatGPT 桌面应用如何运行，包括使用哪个模型提供商（amazon-bedrock）、选择哪个模型，以及权限或上下文限制等设置。

将模型 ID 和具名配置文件（例如 codex-il5）替换为获批的值。

步骤 3：启动、初始化并验证

从 ChatGPT 网站下载并安装应用。安装后保持应用关闭。如果应用自动打开，或此前已启动过，请完全退出 ChatGPT，并结束所有仍在运行的 ChatGPT 或 Codex 进程。

确保首次启动应用之前，requirements.toml 和 config.toml 已就位。

启动应用以加载 requirements.toml 和 config.toml 设置。确保显示的模型提供商为 amazon-bedrock。

在 Codex CLI 中，你应该能看到如下所示的 /status 选项卡：

图 1：Codex CLI 的 /status 选项卡，确认模型提供商为 amazon-bedrock

在 ChatGPT 桌面应用中，你也可以确认模型提供商为 amazon-bedrock。

图 2：ChatGPT 桌面应用设置，显示模型提供商为 amazon-bedrock

故障排查

应用提示登录 OpenAI 账户。请核实 requirements.toml 和 config.toml 使用的位置和文件名与上表完全一致，终止所有 ChatGPT 和 Codex 进程，然后重新启动。这些文件必须在应用启动前就位。

AWS GovCloud (US) 端点被报告为不受支持。请向 OpenAI 确认确切的桌面应用或 app-server 版本、端点和模型。仅更改 URL 并不能使其获得支持。

使用了错误的 AWS 身份。检查实际生效的凭证来源和具名配置文件。检查是否有 Amazon Bedrock API 密钥优先于该配置文件。

功能限制缺失。重启后检查完整的实际生效要求。仅限 API 登录的设置不会应用功能策略。

回滚与清理
